51230.description: In the old tongue of Thavnair, this handsome crab's name means “sweet rose.” Although naturally poisonous, a judicious boiling will neutralize the toxins, providing for a safe, delectable feast.

51231.description: Said to have started life as a fallen strand of Saint Agama's hair, the dried forms of these wavekin are often seen adorning worshipers' garments like parched little talismans.

51232.description: The steely glint of this wavekin's dorsal fins evokes the weapons wielded by Thavnair's temple guardians. Perhaps it too watches over some sacred site in the depths.

51233.description: Long seen as harbingers of inclement weather, this wavekin's name approximates to “rain cloud” in the common tongue. While these fish do indeed tend to appear before storms hit, naturalists posit they are simply fleeing as fast as their little fins will carry them.

51234.description: Though this leviathan is equipped with noteworthy jaws capable of shredding prey to pieces, this scalekin's name actually means “blunt-nosed thief.” Presumably this is a reference to it snatching the lives of any creatures foolish enough to contest its reign in the depths.

51235.description: This ancient reptile inhabits the seas near Thavnair, where it enjoys enduring favor amongst the populace, appearing in folklore and myriad local tales. For despite its glistening maw of razor-sharp teeth, the Thavnasaurus has a remarkably gentle temperament.

51237.description: The semi-crystalline flesh of this grouper results from absorbing a surfeit of aether over its lifespan─most of which it spends swimming at the vanguard of spectral currents.

51238.description: This subspecies is revered as a sign of good fortune in fishing villages across Thavnair. Its boldly patterned flanks are easily visible from above the water's surface, and sightings are said to precipitate a bumper catch for the day.

51239.description: This variety of red mantis displays even more exuberant coloration than its cousins. Though this vivid hue dulls to an ash grey after cooking, the flesh remains simply scrumptious with a pinch of salt.

51240.description: Exposure to spectral currents seems to have further heightened this crustacean's already exceptional beauty─and taste. This pedigree is unambiguously reflected in its name: “resplendent rose,” as well as the fact it is routinely served at the satrap's palace.

51241.description: The distinct pattern adorning the scales of this flat fish resembles the glinting eye of some deep-sea behemoth. Indeed, the illusion is enough to send even wavekin much larger than darpana fleeing in terror.

51242.description: When dried, these slender, sharp-nosed fish make for excellent projectiles. Some Thavnairian merchants have even taken to launching them at wall-mounted maps, planning their next excursion based on where the silver snout pierces the parchment. One wonders how many businesses have floundered as the result of an errant throw.

51243.description: Over the millennia, this ancient species has been much transformed by its time spent traversing spectral currents. In recent years, this specimen has garnered significant attention among Sharlayan scholars devoted to the study of underwater aetheric currents.

51244.description: Although large for mantis shrimp, these tiger-striped crustaceans are extremely timid. They spend much of their time cowering on the seabed, rarely moving unless swept up in a spectral current.

51245.description: This mahi-mahi subspecies moves at an infuriatingly ponderous pace. Seeking sport, some Thavnairian fishers will attempt to harry the creature along, though seldom to any avail. Apparently, even the sight of a fishing boat's prow bearing down upon it isn't enough to rouse a mehi-mahi from its leisurely locomotion.

51246.description: This venerable scalekin is endowed with rows of saw-like teeth, which it uses to terrifying effect in dispatching hapless prey. Mere mention of its name─and the image of those dreadful fangs that inevitably follows─is enough to strike fear into the hearts of veteran fishers, and shred any confidence that mere ilms of timber might keep one safe from harm.

51247.description: With an imposing name befitting a serpent possessing such massive saber-like tusks, Manasvin is heralded in the Near East as a warder of evil spirits─who are presumably as fearful of being skewered as any mortal would be.

51687.description: The calmest, most carefree inhabitant of Thavnairian coastal waters, this wavekin bears the markings of its approximate Hingan namesake: a breezy patterned garment traditionally worn during the warm summer months.

51999.description: Though the name may suggest to Eorzean speakers some association with the leftward direction, rest assured that, unlike its smaller kin, this specimen can only swim toward its right fin. Its appellation instead refers to a chant beloved by fans of a local ball-based sport─who must resist the temptation to send it soaring aloft.

52000.description: Much like its lesser brethren, this formidable fish has a long history of being brandished as a blunt instrument. In the days of Yok Huy conquest, warriors encountering these wavekin in Kozama'uka would snatch the creatures from the shallows, thereby acquiring slippery─and presumably perturbed─cudgels with which to wage war.

52001.description: This large freshwater fish uses its tapered, shovel-like snout to probe the riverbed, hunting for tasty morsels amidst the mud.

52002.description: The flat forms of these wavekin are held to wax and wane in perfect harmony with the moon. In the depths of the Ja Tiika Heartland, where the night sky is shrouded by unbroken canopy, people have long used these creatures as a kind of living calendar.

52003.description: Revered for their role in maintaining the cleanliness of water sources, these slender wavekin are considered symbols of good fortune in Mamook. Such is the reverence for these fortuitous fish that they are traditionally served at the weaning ceremonies of two-headed Mamool Ja infants.

52004.description: These hulking scalekin spend much of their lives in murky brackish waters, flesh slowly steeping in salt. So delicious a prize are these pre-seasoned creatures, hunters will gladly risk life and limb to bring one down.

52005.description: Appearing out of nowhere, borne on sudden, ever-shifting air currents, these tunicates are widely feared as spectral messengers from the dark depths of Zorgor─not to mention their penchant for grabbing the ankles of unwary passersby.

52006.description: This gargantuan shark gleams with the brilliance of burnished copper. Some believe this luster results from a diet rich in Endless and their aether.

52007.description: This wavekin's vibrant flanks call to mind the iridescent strata of Worqor Lar Dor. Indeed, legend has it that the creature began life as a chunk of rock from that mighty edifice that plunged into a lake after being seized by sudden thirst.

52008.description: Rimed with algae and wreathed in foliage, this still, silent hunter lurks in the gloomy substrate of Miyakabek'zu. Intriguingly, the crystalline protrusions on its back share the same internal structure as many precious gems.

52009.description: While Eorzean eyes might associate this wavekin's rounded form with that of a heart, for the Mamool Ja, this revered creature is a symbol of the sky itself─a facet of the firmament glimpsed briefly through the swaying canopy above.

52010.description: Some naturalists believe─against all evidence to the contrary─that rroneek are in fact a species of fish, and point to this ancient horned wavekin as some kind of progenitor. Regardless of one's thoughts on the matter, the creature's horns certainly evoke their land-dwelling namesake.

52011.description: Endowed with three curving, scythe-like fins, this terrifying wavekin is the culmination of experiments to replicate an ancient sea monster. When its creators discovered it could cleave through electrope with unsettling ease, they began to regret their success.

52012.description: Named an “envoy of rainbows” in the Hanuhanu tongue, this fish gleams in seven distinct colors. Its scales are as popular as precious stones when it comes to decoration due to their brilliance and luster.

52013.description: Blooms of these jellyfish can be found off the docks of High Tide Harbor. When dried, their durability and elasticity make them valued packaging amongst traders.

52014.description: Exceedingly agile, this shrimp bears a name evocative of rust and deadly shears. Its tight ruddy-brown carapace conceals flesh bountiful in nourishment.

52015.description: Squid native to the waters beneath Zorgor the Boundless. While the Tonawawta have used its ink as pigment since days of eld, its flesh is considered inedible by even the most ambitious epicureans.

52016.description: This remarkable species breathes by means of lungs, perhaps due to the shoals where it resides. Exhalations are summarily absorbed by the body, which creates enough carbonic acid to trigger a popping noise upon exposure to air.

52297.description: Formed when lesser balls of lightning collide and fuse, these colossal, coruscating specimens are exceptionally volatile. The slightest rupture in its outer membrane can result in a catastrophic discharge of levin─a phenomenon which has left more than one curious naturalist frazzled...or worse.
